author: City News Service
title: Fast-moving brush fire burns hundreds of acres at Camp Pendleton, closes part of Interstate 5 - NewsBreak
text:
By City News Service ,
4 hours ago A fast-moving brush fire blackened hundreds of acres at Camp Pendleton Thursday, threatening structures and prompting evacuations on the grounds of the military base.
The blaze, dubbed the Henderson Fire , erupted shortly before 2 p.m. in the western reaches of the Marine Corps base, close to the intersection of Basilone and Las Pulgas roads, authorities reported.
Just after 5 p.m., the flames had become enough of a potential threat to motorists on the evening commute that authorities briefly closed Interstate 5 in both directions, from Harbor Drive in Oceanside north to Basilone.
Smoke from of the wind-driven Hendeson Fire on Camp Pendleton. (Photo courtesy of Cal Fire) Within an hour, the California Highway Patrol was re-opening the busy stretch of I-5, but also warned that “the highway may be closed again immediately if conditions require.”
Pushed by winds out of the east, the fire charred more than 1,100 acres within two hours, according to Cal Fire, and were moving dangerously close to populated areas of the base, along with power lines.
An evacuation order was issued for the Las Flores, or 41 Area, of the base. All personnel in that zone were directed to evacuate to Paige Field House, in the 11 Area of Camp Pendleton, or to a secondary evacuation point at the 21 Area gym.
There are no evacuations outside of the base as of 5:30 p.m.
Ground crews and personnel aboard firefighting aircraft were working to halt the spread of the Henderson Fire.
As of 4 p.m., there were no reports of structural damage or injuries, but several roads were shut down.
Along with I-5, Las Pulgas between Brown Street and Stuart Mesa Road is closed, as is the Las Pulgas Gate to the base. Only emergency vehicles can use those roadways.
The cause of the fire, which had grown to roughly 400 acres within 90 minutes, is under investigation.
The Henderson Fire has exceeded initial estimates, which predicted the flames would consume 1,000 acres.
Updated 6:30 p.m. Oct. 15, 2026
